\section[programar]{programar — to schedule, to plan; to program}

\label{lesson:ES-C615-programar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the guarantee, then the Spanish for the protection.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: programar}
\textbf{programar} — \textquotedblleft{}to schedule, to plan; to program\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Programamos la reunión para el martes.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We scheduled the meeting for Tuesday.}
\end{quote}

Also to write a computer program.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{programar} is built on \emph{programa}, from Late Latin \emph{programma}, taken from Greek \emph{programma} 'a public notice', from \emph{graphein} 'to write' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{programar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{programar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{programar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the guarantee, then the Spanish for the protection, then say \emph{programar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does programar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To schedule, to plan; to program\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[planificar]{planificar — to plan}

\label{lesson:ES-C615-planificar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the protection, then the Spanish for to schedule.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: planificar}
\textbf{planificar} — \textquotedblleft{}to plan\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Planificamos el viaje con tiempo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We planned the trip in good time.}
\end{quote}

More formal than \emph{planear}. Spelling: \emph{planifiqué}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{planificar} is built on \emph{plan} with the ending \emph{-ificar}; \emph{plan} rests on \emph{plano}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{planus} 'flat' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{planificar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{planificar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{planificar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the protection, then the Spanish for to schedule, then say \emph{planificar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does planificar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To plan\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[el propósito]{el propósito — the purpose, the aim; the resolution}

\label{lesson:ES-C615-proposito}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to schedule, then the Spanish for to plan.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el propósito}
\textbf{el propósito} — \textquotedblleft{}the purpose, the aim; the resolution\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Mi propósito es aprender inglés.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My aim is to learn English.}
\end{quote}

\emph{A propósito} — on purpose; by the way. \emph{Los propósitos de Año Nuevo} — New Year resolutions.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{propósito} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{propositum} 'that which is proposed, an aim', built on \emph{proponere} 'to put forward' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el propósito}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el propósito}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el propósito}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to schedule, then the Spanish for to plan, then say \emph{el propósito} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el propósito mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The purpose, the aim; the resolution\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la intención]{la intención — the intention}

\label{lesson:ES-C615-intencion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to plan, then the Spanish for the purpose.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la intención}
\textbf{la intención} — \textquotedblleft{}the intention\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
No tengo intención de mudarme.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I have no intention of moving house.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Tener la intención de} + infinitive.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{intención} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{intentio} 'a stretching, a purpose', built on \emph{intendere} and \emph{tendere} 'to stretch' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la intención}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la intención}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la intención}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to plan, then the Spanish for the purpose, then say \emph{la intención} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la intención mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The intention\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[proponerse]{proponerse — to set out to, to resolve}

\label{lesson:ES-C615-proponerse}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the purpose, then the Spanish for the intention.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: proponerse}
\textbf{proponerse} — \textquotedblleft{}to set out to, to resolve\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Me propongo correr cada mañana.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I have resolved to run every morning.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Proponerse} + infinitive is to make it your goal.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{proponerse} is built on \emph{proponer}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{proponere} 'to put forward' and rebuilt on \emph{poner} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{proponerse}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{proponerse}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{proponerse}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the purpose, then the Spanish for the intention, then say \emph{proponerse} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[(dialogue)]{Repaso de los capítulos 608–615}

\label{lesson:ES-R615-repaso-608-615}



\begin{quote}
Say the Spanish for to increase and to decrease.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item to increase, to decrease, the increase, the growth, the trend
  \item the progress, to perfect, the challenge, to face, to persevere
  \item the tolerance, to tolerate, the integration, the immigration, the living together
  \item the condition, as long as, unless, provided that, in case
  \item except if, on condition that, otherwise, in that case, in any case
  \item to require, the requirement, the uncertainty, likely, the probability
  \item to prevent, to risk, to guarantee, the guarantee, the protection
  \item to schedule, to plan, the purpose, the intention, to set out to
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
To increase? (\textbf{aumentar}.) To decrease? (\textbf{disminuir}.) The increase? (\textbf{el aumento}.) The growth? (\textbf{el crecimiento}.) The trend? (\textbf{la tendencia}.) The progress? (\textbf{el progreso}.) To perfect? (\textbf{perfeccionar}.) The challenge? (\textbf{el desafío}.) To face? (\textbf{afrontar}.) To persevere? (\textbf{perseverar}.) The tolerance? (\textbf{la tolerancia}.) To tolerate? (\textbf{tolerar}.) The integration? (\textbf{la integración}.) The immigration? (\textbf{la inmigración}.) The living together? (\textbf{la convivencia}.) The condition? (\textbf{la condición}.) As long as? (\textbf{siempre que}.) Unless? (\textbf{a menos que}.) Provided that? (\textbf{con tal de que}.) In case? (\textbf{en caso de que}.) Except if? (\textbf{a no ser que}.) On condition that? (\textbf{a condición de que}.) Otherwise? (\textbf{de lo contrario}.) In that case? (\textbf{en ese caso}.) In any case? (\textbf{en todo caso}.) To require? (\textbf{requerir}.) The requirement? (\textbf{el requisito}.) The uncertainty? (\textbf{la incertidumbre}.) Likely? (\textbf{probable}.) The probability? (\textbf{la probabilidad}.) To prevent? (\textbf{prevenir}.) To risk? (\textbf{arriesgar}.) To guarantee? (\textbf{garantizar}.) The guarantee? (\textbf{la garantía}.) The protection? (\textbf{la protección}.) To schedule? (\textbf{programar}.) To plan? (\textbf{planificar}.) The purpose? (\textbf{el propósito}.) The intention? (\textbf{la intención}.) To set out to? (\textbf{proponerse}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
